 Jeremiah Smith Is That Good, So Which NFL Teams Could Consider Trading Up for Star WR in 2027 Draft
 Brent Sobleski Nov 21, 2026 
 Calvin Johnson, AJ Green, Julio Jones and Ja'Marr Chase are the best wide receiver prospects over the last 25 years. None of them were the No. 1 overall pick in their respective draft classes. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith is on par with all four as a prospect and possibly even better. NFL teams should be falling over themselves to try to acquire his services. 
 Currently, Smith holds the highest grade the Bleacher Report Scouting Report has ever assigned in its seven cycles of evaluating collegiate talent. At 9.9 (out of 10), the wide receiver is considered a near-perfect prospect. 
 Take a quick look at Smith's scouting report , courtesy of B/R's Dame Parson , and realize he's the ideal NFL receiver. Here are the highlights: 
 - NFL body, frame and sturdy build to create advantageous physical matchups.
- Intentional route-runner with violent steps and snappiness out of his breaks.
- Powerful strider with top-end speed to attack and exploit the vertical plane.
- Incredible strength and reliable hands; rarely drops passes.
- Outstanding ball-tracking down the field, shows late hands and reaches another level of aggressiveness once the ball is in the air.
 Smith already broke the Big Ten Conference's all-time receiving yardage and touchdown records before his true junior season had even come to a close. 
 With a quarterback almost certainly going No. 1 overall due to demand at the position, Smith's skill set should be up for sale, with numerous organizations jockeying to trade up for a pass-catcher. 
The Los Angeles Chargers, who currently own next year's second overall pick, could easily select Smith and happily move on without thinking twice. Or, the organization can get a windfall of draft picks to address multiple roster issues and kickstart the team's rebuild. 
Five specific franchises are within striking distance based on the current draft order that should be desperate to trade up for Smith. 
 Miami Dolphins
 1 of 5 AP Photo/Zach Bolinger Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas 
 Current Draft Slot : Third overall
The Miami Dolphins could find themselves in a difficult position based on how the draft order currently sits. Everything will depend on how the organization wants to move forward at quarterback. 
Malik Willis was placed in a near-impossible position this season due to the lack of talent around the quarterback position. Injuries have only made the situation worse. Willis now finds himself on injured reserve. 
The Dolphins have two pathways to pursue this offseason. Either the front office builds around Willis, or the team chooses to go all-in on another quarterback. Miami could easily be the franchise trying to move up for the No. 1 overall pick to draft Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker. If that doesn't happen, the Dolphins' decision-makers should do everything in their power to obtain Smith, even if that means swapping picks to move up one spot. 
Miami drafted three wide receivers in this year's class, but the team can't stop there since none of them should be considered legitimate No. 1 targets. 
Whatever the Dolphins eventually do at quarterback, a weapon of Smith's caliber will greatly help whoever is behind center. Furthermore, Miami's lineup simply needs a playmaker and an infusion of talent. Thus, drafting arguably the best wide receiver prospect of all time should be a priority. 
 Philadelphia Eagles
 2 of 5 AP Photo/Matt Rourke Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith 
 Current Draft Slot : Fifth overall
Should Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman trade up to draft a wide receiver for a third time? Yes.
That idea isn't an indictment of DeVonta Smith or rookie Makai Lemon. Instead, the approach is all about taking advantage of a significant opportunity if it's presented.
Due to this season going off the rails, the Eagles currently own a top-five draft pick. Philadelphia hasn't selected that high since trading up for Carson Wentz in the 2016 class. In fact, Roseman isn't shy about making a move, even if it's a minimal trade-up, to ensure the team lands a specific talent. See: Carter, Jalen. 
Much like Carter, Jeremiah Smith can completely change the complexion of the Eagles' roster, especially on offense. What the team lost when it traded AJ Brown can be reinserted with a younger, more explosive version. Thus, a trio of Jeremiah Smith, DeVonta Smith and Lemon will be extremely difficult to defend, with each placed in specific roles to maximize their skill sets. 
Furthermore, the Eagles still don't know exactly how they'll progress at quarterback beyond this position. If Jalen Hurts is medically cleared and ready to return, more weapons in the passing game will help prevent the intermittent offensive stagnation that has plagued the Eagles during the last two seasons. Even without Hurts, a wide receiver corps consisting of those three targets will make anyone better. 
 Washington Commanders
 3 of 5 AP Photo/Adam Hunger Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels 
 Current Draft Slot : 11th overall
 The Washington Commanders' offseason plan should be relatively simple: Do whatever is necessary to improve Jayden Daniels' surrounding cast. A legitimate No. 1 target can only help the young quarterback's development. 
 Stefon Diggs currently leads the Commanders with 36 receptions for 386 yards. Those numbers rank 43rd and 50th overall, respectively. Washington's top wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, is already out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, a difficult injury from which to bounce back, particularly for a 31-year-old wide receiver. Furthermore, four of the team's wide receivers—Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, Van Jefferson and Diggs, who turns 33 next weekend—are free agents after this season. 
 Washington requires a reset among its skill positions. Jeremiah Smith is the perfect piece to serve as the starting point. 
 However, the Commanders' front office may have agreed upon a significant deal to target the class's WR1 since Washington currently sits just outside the 2027 draft's Top 10. Deals of this nature have happened before. A handful of teams may consider a talent of Smith's caliber. However, a pair of first-round picks will likely be the starting point for any conversation. He's worth it, though.

 Bleacher Report 20h Baltimore Ravens
 4 of 5 AP Photo/Nick Wass Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers 
 Current Draft Slot : 14th overall
The Baltimore Ravens are losing ground in the AFC North and the conference itself. At the same time, a down season should serve as a chance for self-reflection. 
An injury to quarterback Lamar Jackson certainly hasn't helped matters. Even so, the Ravens must consider a change in their approach. Running back Derrick Henry turns 33 in January. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley, who also turns 33 next year, is no longer playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level. Tight end Mark Andrews will turn 32 during the 2027 season. A handful of other aging veterans are pending free agents as well. 
Next offseason will be the ideal time for the organization to reassess its setup and head in a different direction. To do so, the team must add legitimate talent. 
Zay Flowers is an excellent wide receiver. He currently ranks 12th overall with 688 receiving yards despite the Ravens' starting four different quarterbacks. However, Flowers has some limitations due to his size and build. A strong move to trade up for Jeremiah Smith will finally give Jackson two big-time options in the passing game. 
Jackson's mobility will always be a part of his game. However, the team's continued run-first mentality hasn't allowed it to achieve anything of significance. 
 Instead, the Ravens could finally open up their offense to a greater degree. A trade-up for Smith will certainly make a statement. That version of the Ravens won't be the same ol' Ravens. The franchise will finally be going in a new direction and placing more emphasis on Jackson. 
 Las Vegas Raiders
 5 of 5 AP Photo/Jeff Lewis Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza 
 Current Draft Slot : 15h overall
 A strong start to the season has placed the Las Vegas Raiders further down the draft order than what's usually seen. However, the team lost six of its last seven games and moved on from veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins in favor of this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. 
 The latter point is important because the rookie will face multiple top defenses during Las Vegas' next seven games—which means a turnaround could be difficult. Mendoza's maturation is also crucial to the Raiders' long-term organizational health. 
The Raiders' current wide receiver options are underwhelming at best. Tight end Brock Bowers is the team's No. 1 receiving threat, of course. The thought of Bowers playing alongside Jeremiah Smith would be straight nightmare fuel for opposing defensive coordinators. Thus, general manager John Spytek should be ultra-aggressive and go all in to help the reigning Heisman Trophy winner and his team reach its full potential. 
A possible trade-up may not be quite as expensive depending on how the rest of the Raiders' season goes. Their draft slotting could easily end up around the 10th overall pick. Even so, some type of move will be necessary for Smith. The Raiders may be missing pieces at other positions, but a set of triplets featuring Mendoza, Bowers and Smith could be absolutely dynamic.
